recipes.name: Asian Cucumber Salad
ingredients_raw: 2 cucumbers - halved lengthwise, seeded, and sliced

steps.text: Place cucumber slices in a colander and sprinkle with salt; set aside to drain while you prepare the remaining ingredients.
Whisk vinegar and sugar together in a small bowl until sugar is dissolved; stir in sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and sesame seeds.
Rinse salt off cucumber slices by running under cold water; place in a large bowl.
Add sliced red chili peppers and vinegar dressing; toss to coat. Cover and refrigerate the salad until ready to serve. This salad tastes best on the day it is made.

raw_recipe.headline: Asian Cucumber Salad
raw_recipe.description: A refreshing Asian cucumber salad made with slices of crunchy cucumber and chili tossed in a ginger, garlic, sesame, and rice vinegar dressing.

video.description: This video shows you how to cut cucumbers into mesmerizing spiral shapes and thin, flat ribbons to make Asian Cucumber Salad. In this refreshing salad recipe, a zesty, salty-sweet dressing – featuring rice vinegar and sugar plus grated garlic and ginger – coats cucumbers that have been covered with salt, then rinsed. Prepare this fresh salad as a tasty summer snack, or serve as a side dish at dinner.

review.reviewBody: Some of my all-time favorite ingredients in one bowl! I've made it twice this week, and it's fail proof. Used green Thai peppers (very hot!) but I think the red ones would be more aesthetically pleasing. Second time I made it i used 3 cukes because the first time there was a lot of leftover dressing. Perfect for a late dinner salad.

The recipe was good. The cucumbers were sprinkled with some salt but not a lot. Waited 45 minutes and rinsed them thoroughly. It removed all the salt. Patted dry with paper towels. I used 1/2 the recommended red peppers and it was fine. I learned from other reviews, the dressing was too much. I made 1/2 of the recipe dressing amount and it was enough. I added some thin sliced tomato to the salad. Everyone liked the salad, and I had no leftovers. This is a family favorite to go with beef bulgogi in lettuce cups.

A great recipe BUT after salting the cucumber and letting it sit for an hour in a colander, I tried to rinse off the salt with cold water, as per the recipe instructions. I let the cold water run for 3 minutes and then patted (petted? :)) the cucumbers dry, but the cucumbers were still too salty. I went ahead and made the dressing and the rice vinegar DID cut the salt taste, but not by much.
A very tasty recipe but next time I will not salt the cucumber at all.

Delicious salad. I used a mandolin but I think this made the slices to thin and kind of wimpy so next time I'll be slicing thinker. 

I added red onion which I think really made the dish both asthetically pleasing and yummy. I soaked the onions in the vinegar for a bit to kill of some of the harsh onion flavor which sometimes overtakes a dish when using uncooked onion. Just left it sitting in the vinegar while I cut up the ginger and allowed the cucumbers to dehydrate. I also just added a sprinkling of crushed red peppers (why take a trip to the store when I had everything else! lol) instead of red chilis. Came out perfect.

I love the Asian cucumber salad in Thai restaurants and was eager to try this. I made it for Easter dinner and it was a huge success! I used the mandolin to slice the cucumbers very thin and didn't have peppers so used red pepper flakes instead. Also I substituted Stevia in place of sugar since I'm trying to be low carb! I was looking forward to leftovers but sadly, there wasn't a lot!

I reduced the salad dressing by half and still had quite a bit of it. I added some red onion and was glad i did because it might have been a bit bland without it. The dressing is very good, I did use fresh ginger and garlic and let the salad marinate for about three hours before eating. Served with Honey Ginger Salmon on this website.

The dressing is spot-on to what I've had in restaurants. I made the dressing and let it chill in the fridge by itself for a few hours first. Then about an hour before I served, I mixed in the dressing with the veggies. You probably only need to make half the dressing for this amount of cucumber. I added in some green onion and cilantro - yum!

I halved it, using half an English cucumber, thinly slicing and not peeling and adding chopped scallions. As others mentioned, there was a lot of liquid, so I just drained some off. Cut back a bit on the sesame oil because it can be a strong flavor and you can always add more. No fresh ginger so added a few shakes of dry and red pepper flakes in place of the chile peppers. Very good with leftover Asian Lettuce Wraps (without lettuce!) from this site (and highly recommended) and sesame ginger rice. A nice complement to Asian-inspired dishes, especially the spicier ones! Thanks sandradxb!
Enjoyable dish I added sliced cherry tomatoes, match stick carrots , dried crushed red peppers 1/2 teaspoon, 1/2 of garlic crushed or less than recipe stated.

Light and refreshing summer salad. Perfect to serve with either lunch or dinner. I couldn't find the peppers, so took the advice of other reviewers and used green onions and red pepper flakes. It was delicious. If possible, chill both the dressing and the sweated cucumbers. Delicious when served chilled.

i've made this many times and its the best! tastes very authentic to what i've had in japanese restaurants. if i don't have ginger or garlic or sugar i use the powdered kind and honey and its still good. very vital that you use seasoned rice wine vinegar and that you let the cucs drain and rinse! once i forgot to rinse and the recipe was still good but tasted more like pickles/garnish than a salad.
Absolutely love it%!
It was delicious

I made this for an Independence Day celebration potluck. It was a good alternative salad to contrast with the usual potato and pasta salads. I used English cucumbers so I didn't de-seed them. I also didn't find the hot peppers I wanted so I used some red bell pepper and 2 teaspoons gochugaru (Korean pepper flakes). It was a hit.
I made this recipe as a side dish for Penang Pork Satay. I followed the instructions and used all of the ingredients. I used hot Fresno chiles.
We didn’t care for this. It was too sweet and could have used more acid or something.
I put only 1 Tbs of sesame oil, and I used red pepper flakes. Really good
Great flavors. Everyone loved it.

Very good drsg. I didnt have fresh ginger & will have it on hand when making another batch. Left out the hot peppers & substituted a dash of hot paprika. Toasted the sesame seeds. Very nice & light drsg. I think this would make a good green salad drsg or poured over oriental noodles.
My absolute favorite cucumber salad!
